title: Noether at the frontier
eyebrow: CETI · AI-STORIES · Noether at the frontier · part 3
lede: Machines that find the number that never changes, the numbers hidden inside a network that learns, and the open question of whether anything like it holds for knowledge: 30,000 recall dots, 24,000 training dots, a toy of 3 questions and a tree of 19. Part 3 of 3.

chapters.title: A dot cannot leave its shell
Reorder the parts of a question

captions: Last time, a dot could not leave its shell.
Each shell is a number that never changes.
Take the rule away. Plot only where things are.
Each dot is one moment of one orbit.
That is 30,000 moments, tangled, with no rule.
A computer hunts for any number that stays put.
It lands on the same shells, told nothing.
In 2021, a team tried this on 5 test systems.
It found every number that truly never changes.
It also flagged numbers that only nearly hold.
Small, clean systems, and the laws were known.
Now something that learns: a small network.
Each dot: one neuron, one moment of training.
24,000 dots, tangled like before.
Plot each by one sum of its neuron's weights.
Each network here has 8 neurons.
Each neuron keeps one sum fixed: 8 in all.
Now let it train. Every dot starts to slide.
They slide, but never change layer.
Bigger steps, and the layers start to leak.
The fixed sums hold only for tiny steps.
Now try it on questions.
3 questions that don't need each other.
They can be asked in 6 orders.
The total is 20 in every order.
A model that cares about order contradicts itself.
Reordering cost more than 30 % in some tests.
Our program starts with a tree of questions.
19 questions, in 3 layers.
4 broad, 8 narrower, 7 narrowest.
Behind it: 9 modules and 22 sources.
A claim that survives reordering is a candidate.
Monday: reorder a question's parts. Same answer?

brand.takeaway: Ask what stays when the order changes.

sources: S1
Part 1 package: factory/topics/noether-symmetry/{data/orbit_table.json, recompute.py}: 300 orbits x 100 moments, Kepler states rebuilt by the film. Simulation, tagged SIMULATED on stage.
S2

Liu and Tegmark, Machine learning conservation laws from trajectories (AI Poincare), Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 180604 (2021), arXiv 2011.04698: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.04698 . Abstract: five Hamiltonian systems incl. the three-body problem; recovered all exactly conserved quantities. Not opened here (egress).
S3
Liu, Madhavan, Tegmark, Machine learning conservation laws from differential equations (AI Poincare 2.0), Phys. Rev. E 106, 045307 (2022), arXiv 2203.12610. Context only, nothing on screen.
S4

Du, Hu, Lee, Algorithmic regularization in learning deep homogeneous models: layers are automatically balanced, NeurIPS 2018, arXiv 1806.00900; Kunin, Sagastuy-Brena, Ganguli, Yamins, Tanaka, Neural Mechanics, ICLR 2021, arXiv 2012.04728 (symmetries give conservation laws during training, 'analogous to Noether's theorem'; finite learning rates break them): https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04728
S5
Tanaka and Kunin, Noether's learning dynamics, NeurIPS 2021, arXiv 2105.02716. Context only.
S6

Marcotte, Gribonval, Peyre, Abide by the Law and Follow the Flow: Conservation Laws for Gradient Flows, NeurIPS 2023 (oral), arXiv 2307.00144: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00144 . Counting the independent laws by the Lie algebra generated by the Jacobian's gradient fields. The count 8 for this toy is recomputed here (recompute.py C); the paper's tables are NOT opened (E1).
S7

Chen, Chi, Wang, Zhou (Google DeepMind), Premise Order Matters in Reasoning with Large Language Models, ICML 2024, PMLR 235:6596-6620, arXiv 2402.08939: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.08939 . Abstract: permuting the premise order can cause a performance drop of over 30%.
S8

The owner's course: /home/user/manutej/noether-operadic-course/index.html (README.md; parts/*.js hold the same HTML). Counts: 9 modules, 19 question-tree nodes (4/8/7), 22 sources, counted on disk; quotes in sources.md.
S9
The owner's thesis section 8 'Towards Noether structure on QA-graphs (program, not theorem)' and Module 6 in the same file: the program's own statement of what is not proved.

factory/topics/noether-frontier/recompute.py, seed 20261012 (numpy only): the recall count, the blind search, the training clouds and the count of laws, the toy, the course counts. Simulation, tagged SIMULATED / ILLUSTRATION on stage.
In-film toy of three independent sub-answers (4, 7, 9): numbers chosen by the author, arithmetic only. Tagged ILLUSTRATION on stage; not data.
honest: Nobody has proved a Noether theorem for questions; this is a program, not a result.
lay: OUR DOTS, FADED · THE RESULT IS THEIRS
panel: KUNIN ET AL. · MARCOTTE ET AL.
monday: Ask your AI the same question with its parts
in another order. Does the answer stay?
